sentences.text: Titanonarke was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
This ancient ray belongs to the family Narcinidae, a group of electric rays known today.
A fossilized embryo found inside one specimen proves that this species gave birth to live young.
Analysis of stomach contents reveals it ate an extinct large benthic foraminifera genus called Alveolina.
The genus was first described by Carvalho in the year 2010.
Two distinct species, T. molini and T. megapterygia, are known from the Bolca Lagerstatte in Italy.
Exceptional preservation of multiple whole individuals allowed scientists to reconstruct the lives of these rays.
The fossils contain various life stages and even preserved parasitic isopods attached to the bodies.
Titanonarke likely inhabited shallow waters near coral reefs, similar to its modern relatives.
Titanonarke lived during the Ypresian age of the Eocene epoch.
This period occurred between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian.
